## Biography

PhD McGill 2023. Joined Concordia as a postdoc with the Centre for Pattern Recognition and Machine Intelligence in late 2023, co-supervised by Prof. Sabine Bergler. South Asian heritage; her research community-builds with diasporic communities in Tiohtià:ke/Montréal. Currently applying for first independent NSERC funding while on the academic job market.

## Personal Statement

I am a postdoctoral fellow in machine learning at the Centre for Pattern Recognition and Machine Intelligence at Concordia University. My research is in natural language processing for low-resource South Asian languages.

**Why this area matters:** Most NLP advances ride on English and a handful of other high-resource languages. The 1.7 billion speakers of South Asian languages — Bengali, Tamil, Urdu, Sinhala, and others — face a steep accuracy gap on every modern system, and the gap widens as state-of-the-art models scale on training data those languages cannot access. Closing it requires not just more data, but evaluation standards built with the language communities themselves.

**Why my particular research matters in that area:** I have built two of the first openly-released benchmark suites for Bengali and Tamil NLP, working with linguists and community translators to ensure cultural and dialect coverage. Both are in active use by 30+ research groups internationally. The work shifted from a single benchmark to a methodology for community-validated low-resource evaluation, which is what I now plan to develop into an independent program.

Looking ahead, I am working toward an independent research program at Concordia developing privacy-preserving, community-co-designed NLP tools for diasporic South Asian communities in Tiohtià:ke/Montréal, in partnership with Concordia's Centre for Engineering in Society.

## Supervisory & Mentorship Activities

**Total mentees (last 5 years):** **PhD:** 0 · **Masters:** 1 · **Undergrad/Capstone:** 4 · **Postdoc:** 0

### Group 1 — Undergraduate research mentorship

- **Training philosophy:** Structure first, autonomy second. I onboard undergraduate research assistants with explicit milestone scaffolding for the first 6 weeks, then progressively hand over project ownership as their confidence grows.
- **Training environment:** Weekly 30-minute one-on-one with each RA, plus an open Slack channel for technical questions. Shared writing happens in Overleaf; code happens through GitHub Classroom with mandatory pair-review.
- **EDI practices:** I recruit from Concordia's WiCS (Women in Computer Science) and the Computer Science Undergraduate Society. I do not require prior research experience — only basic CS coursework and curiosity. Two of my four current RAs are first-generation university students.
- **Awards / career outcomes:** Two of four undergraduate RAs have gone on to graduate programs (McGill MSc, U of T MSc). One was a 2024 NSERC USRA recipient on a project I co-designed; another won a Concordia Undergraduate Conference research prize for the BanglaBench dialect work.
